$comment: The declared size of this repository's negative proof. `gate-negative-proof.sh` asks whether a proof EXISTS; its own docstring says counting files cannot judge whether a battery is any good, and that is true. What counting files CAN answer is whether the proof got SMALLER, and until this file nothing did. Measured 2026-09-01: moving `fixtures/findings/bad/26-*.json` and its `.expected` sidecar out of the tree took gate-findings-artifact.sh from 30 artifacts to 29 and it signed VERDICT 0. A negative proof was retired and every gate stayed green. Retiring a control and hiding it are the same edit, so the size of the proof is now a declared limit rather than an invisible fact, and this file lives under `scripts/gates/data/**`, which G7 protects.
$comment_why_exact: Equality in BOTH directions, like gate-agent-roster.sh. Fewer on disk than declared means a proof was retired and the declaration is the only record that it existed. More on disk than declared means the declaration stopped being a baseline - a number nobody updates is a number nobody can be caught by. The chore is one integer per pull request that adds or removes a fixture, and that is the price of the deletion never being silent.
$comment_counted: Per family under `scripts/gates/fixtures/<family>/`: `inputs` counts files under `bad/` or `unmeasurable/` (the cases that make a gate fail or refuse to measure); `assertions` counts `.expected` sidecars (what the failure must SAY). Files under `good/` are not counted here - they are the conformance reference, and `gate-negative-proof.sh` does not rest on them.
